quotes.text: I repent me much , That so I harry'd him
quotes.reference: c. 1606–1607 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Anthonie and Cleopatra”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London: […] Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, (please specify the act number in uppercase Roman numerals, and the scene number in lowercase Roman numerals):

senses.definition: To make repeated attacks on an enemy.

quotes.text: 'One kiss, my bonny sweetheart, I'm after a prize to-night, / But I shall be back with the yellow gold before the morning light; / Yet, if they press me sharply, and harry me through the day, / Then look for me by moonlight, / Watch for me by moonlight, / I'll come to thee by moonlight, though Hell should bar the way.'
quotes.reference: 1906 August, Alfred Noyes, “The Highwayman”, in Poems, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., published October 1906, →OCLC, part 1, stanza V, page 47:
1855–1859, Washington Irving, The Life of George Washington:

quotes.text: A red squirrel had harried the nest of a wood thrush.
quotes.reference: 1896, John Burroughs, Birds and bees and other studies in nature:

senses.definition: To harass, bother or distress with demands, threats, or criticism.

quotes.text: Chelsea also struggled to keep possession as QPR harried and chased at every opportunity, giving their opponents no time on the ball.
quotes.reference: 2011 October 23, Becky Ashton, “QPR 1 – 0 Chelsea”, in BBC Sport:

quotes.text: The Colombians' ire was raised even more 10 minutes later when the referee showed a yellow card to [James] Rodríguez – who was apoplectic at the decision – for an innocuous trip that was, as Rodríguez vociferously pointed out with multiple hand gestures, a first offense compared with Fernandinho's harrying.
quotes.reference: 2014 July 5, Sam Borden, “For bellicose Brazil, payback carries heavy price: Loss of Neymar [International New York Times version: Brazil and referee share some blame for Neymar's injury: Spaniard's failure to curb early pattern of fouls is seen as major factor (7 July 2014, p. 13)]”, in The New York Times:

senses.definition: (India, obsolete) A menial servant; a sweeper.
